summary: Introduced one effective tune CPU resolver and routed its value to both the rendered Slurm directive and default Slurm submission options. Focused rendering and Slurm tests pass; the required configuration/iteration regression command remains partially blocked by two pre-existing iteration-tracking failures unrelated to this change.

files_changed.summary: Resolve effective tune CPUs once and pass the resolved value to script rendering and default Slurm adapter construction.
Verify default submission options and the rendered tune script both request 24 CPUs when scheduler CPUs are 4 and tuning n_procs is 24.
Document the tune workflow's single effective CPU-resolution boundary.

tests_changed.summary: Covers parity between default Slurm submission CPUs and the rendered #SBATCH CPU directive.

checks.summary: All focused tune rendering, default submission, injected-adapter, and generic Slurm adapter tests passed.

Configuration tests passed, but the combined command reported two existing iteration-tracking failures: a full-PA calibration-policy expectation and a fixture writing to a missing remote_data/active directory. Neither failure exercises the TASK-002 CPU changes.

checks.procedure: Inspect the final run_tune_trees call graph, _resolve_effective_tune_cpus, _render_tune_job_script, _build_default_adapters, and the focused submission-parity test.
checks.summary: run_tune_trees computes one effective CPU value and passes it explicitly to both rendering and default adapter construction; other adapter call sites retain scheduler defaults.
All Python source compiled successfully with the compatible repository virtualenv.
No whitespace errors were found in the staged TASK-002 diff.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: One shared resolver determines the effective tune-job CPU count used by both rendering and default Slurm adapter construction.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: VER-T002-03 confirms _resolve_effective_tune_cpus is called once and its result is passed to both consumers.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: With scheduler cpus=4 and impedance n_procs=24, the rendered script and submitted Slurm options both request 24 CPUs.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: VER-T002-01 passes the focused regression that parses the default sbatch preview and compares it with #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=24.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Injected scheduler adapters remain supported and existing tune workflow tests pass.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: VER-T002-01 covers the focused injected-adapter/tune tests, but VER-T002-02 remains red because the broader iteration-tracking suite has two unrelated baseline failures.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Architecture documentation explains that the workflow, not the generic Slurm adapter, owns effective tune CPU resolution.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: VER-T002-03 and the modified architecture documentation describe the workflow-owned resolver and unchanged generic adapter behavior.

deviations.description: The required VER-T002-02 regression command did not pass in the integrated baseline.
deviations.reason: Two failures are outside TASK-002: one existing full-PA calibration-policy expectation and one fixture path setup failure.
deviations.impact: The implementation is scoped and focused verification passes, but the Builder cannot claim a fully green required regression suite without resolving those baseline issues.

unresolved_issues.description: tests/test_iteration_tracking.py still has the two failures reported by VER-T002-02.
unresolved_issues.impact: The combined configuration/iteration regression command remains non-zero.
unresolved_issues.recommended_action: Have the owning workflow/test task reconcile the calibration-policy expectation and create the missing remote_data/active fixture directory, then rerun VER-T002-02.

commit.message: Align tune CPU rendering and submission
